title: Fugitive Charged in UK Murder Still Eludes India Police
excerpt: Pankaj Lamba, charged with killing wife Harshita Brella in Corby, was spotted on CCTV in Gurgaon six months after her death.
body:
Six months after 24-year-old Harshita Brella was found strangled inside a car boot in east London, her accused husband Pankaj Lamba remains a fugitive — last spotted withdrawing money from a bank near Delhi while an international manhunt intensifies.

**What happened:**
Harshita, who had moved to Corby, Northamptonshire after an arranged marriage in 2024, was reported missing on November 13 after her family in Delhi lost contact with her. Police found her body in the early hours of November 14 inside the boot of a silver Vauxhall Corsa abandoned on Brisbane Road in Ilford, east London — some 145 kilometres from her home. A post-mortem confirmed she had been manually strangled. In March 2025, the Crown Prosecution Service charged Lamba in his absence with murder, two counts of rape, sexual assault, and controlling or coercive behaviour.

**A case that has exposed systemic failures:**
The Independent Office for Police Conduct found that Northamptonshire Police missed multiple opportunities to protect Harshita, who had reported abuse repeatedly in the months before her death. Four British officers now face misconduct proceedings. Meanwhile, Delhi High Court Justice Sachin Datta publicly described the Delhi Police investigation as showing 'utter incompetence' after Lamba was captured on CCTV withdrawing over £4,000 from banks in Gurgaon in broad daylight in March 2025. His sister and two relatives — including a suspended Delhi Police officer — have since been detained. A £500 reward has been announced for information leading to his arrest.

**What to watch:**
Lamba's next court hearing is scheduled for August 13, and the Brella family is pushing India's Delhi High Court to transfer the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation — a move that could finally force a credible arrest.
